Gateway to Modern Luxury: Inside the Redesigned 2026 BMW X3

The BMW X3 has long stood as one of the brand's best-selling luxury SUVs, serving as the primary entry point for buyers starting their BMW ownership journey. Fully redesigned for the 2025/2026 model years, the new X3 debuts a distinct exterior aesthetic heavily influenced by BMW’s futuristic Neue Klasse design language. Up front, modern flat kidney grilles and re-engineered headlights extend into the front wings, providing an aggressive, forward-looking stance.

Inside, the X3 inherits high-end cabin architecture previously reserved for flagship models like the 5 Series and 7 Series. Central to the redesign is a multi-input BMW Curved Display running touch, iDrive rotary dial, and voice controls, framed by a striking diamond-cut ambient light strip spanning the dashboard and door panels. Africa’s richest person Aliko Dangote, is opening up his privately controlled oil refinery to public shareholders on Monday, September 14 for the first time in what is expected to be the biggest IPO in the continent’s history. The cement magnate is offering individual investors up to 4.1 billion shares (or 3.3% of the company) at 40 cents each (525 Nigerian Naira), with the order book closing on October 13 at a 10-share buy minimum, an exceptionally low entry requirement of roughly $4. The stock is expected to start trading on the Nigerian Stock Exchange in November.

“We have D-Day on Monday,” Dangote recently told Forbes, explaining how he didn’t know until very late when exactly the IPO would get underway so will now be late to an investment summit in Canada that he promised Prime Minister Mark Carney he’d attend.
